title: Citing ProPublica, Lawmakers Introduce Bill to Help U.S. Citizens Sue ICE for Wrongful Detentions
author: Nicole Foy
content:
**What Happened:** A New Mexico Democrat in the House [introduced a
bill](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/10826/text) last
week that would make it easier for U.S. citizens to sue immigration agents and
the federal government over wrongful detentions and arrests.

Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández credited ProPublica’s reporting as the catalyst
for the bill, the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act. Earlier
this month, we revealed that more than [500 U.S. citizens have been detained
in warrantless arrests](https://projects.propublica.org/american-citizens-
detained-dhs-civil-rights/) during the second Trump administration.

Leger Fernández said the
[legislation](https://fernandez.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=665)
would roll back the protections from lawsuits that agents and the federal
government currently have. It would also establish a minimum level of
compensation for people who win their suits, and extend the statute of
limitations for such cases.

The legislation would also take back any unspent Immigration and Customs
Enforcement funding from President Donald Trump’s so-called One Big Beautiful
Bill Act.

Leger Fernández’s bill was introduced with co-sponsor Rep. Bonnie Watson
Coleman, a New Jersey Democrat.

**Why It Matters:** It can be difficult to sue federal officers for wrongful
arrests or excessive force, or for [local prosecutors to bring
charges](https://www.propublica.org/article/why-local-state-police-rarely-
investigate-ice-cbp-fbi). Federal agents can claim immunity in response to
civil lawsuits or to state charges and can move their cases to federal court.

People who accuse immigration agents of wrongdoing can currently only[ sue in
a narrow set of circumstances, and
p](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/why-it-is-difficult-sue-ice-
agents-2026-01-15/)revious [Democratic bills](https://www.edmarkey.com/boston-
globe-in-wake-of-ice-shooting-markey-and-pressley-introduce-bill-to-end-
federal-law-enforcement-immunity/) aiming to [change
that](https://www.whitehouse.senate.gov/news/release/whitehouse-johnson-
introduce-pair-of-bills-to-hold-federal-law-enforcement-accountable-for-
constitutional-violations/) have not passed.

Some local prosecutors have announced [investigations into the wrongful
arrests](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/ramsey-county-officials-sue-
homeland-security-over-chongly-scott-thao-arrest-investigation/) of U.S.
citizens or [prosecuted federal agents](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-
news/ice-agent-appears-in-federal-court-on-gun-brandishing-charges/) accused
of wrongdoing during immigration enforcement actions.

**What They Said:** In an interview with ProPublica, Leger Fernández
emphasized that accountability could not only address past wrongs, it may also
help head them off in the future. “We know that when there are consequences,
bad actors start behaving better because they don't want to face those
consequences,” she said.

Without legislation, Leger Fernández said, agents “will continue to violate
the law, to violate their own policy, and to violate the Constitution without
any consequences.”

Asked about the legislation, the Department of Homeland Security, ICE’s parent
agency, repeated claims that it is not arresting U.S. citizens and defended
its immigration operations as “highly targeted.”

**Background:** The federal government denies that there is any pattern of
immigration agents detaining U.S. citizens, but according to ProPublica’s
count, more than 100 citizens were held after agents questioned their
citizenship. At least 70 children and teens were also detained.

Last year, congressional Democrats [announced a wide-ranging investigation
into immigration agents’ detention of U.S.
citizens](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-ice-americans-
detained-joint-congressional-investigation) after our earlier investigation
found that [more than 170 citizens were detained by immigration
agents](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-dhs-american-citizens-
arrested-detained-against-will).
